subject: Post-call: HIPAA/BAA eligibility & next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-call: HIPAA/BAA eligibility & next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of conversation:
- MedWise is evaluating Redwood for a PHI-processing workload (clinical summarization + triage).
- Primary compliance asks: BAA, US data residency, SOC 2 proof, KMS/HSM integration, model training restrictions, and an initial security questionnaire.

What Redwood can confirm today:
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I and is actively working toward SOC 2 Type II (Type II expected Q3 2026). We can share our SOC 2 readiness summary + timeline.
- BAA availability: We offer BAA options for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). For Hosted API, BAAs are considered on a case-by-case enterprise contract basis and typically require VPC/private-networking + strict data retention controls.
- PHI handling boundaries: PHI processing is supported on Dedicated and Private modes where customers can enforce encryption keys (KMS/HSM), disable persistent logging of request bodies, and control retention. We do not use customer request data to train models unless a customer explicitly opts-in.
- Data residency: Dedicated/Private deployments can be provisioned in specific cloud regions (US-only).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send over an initial security questionnaire response and a Redwood BAA template for your legal/security to review.
2) Dev will provide the technical confirmation on KMS, audit logs, and training policies.
3) Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security/infosec team Wednesday 5/20 at 11am PT?

Attachments I’ll send: preliminary questionnaire response (stub), BAA template, and SOC 2 readiness summary.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the docs in a separate email.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: HIPAA/BAA eligibility & next steps

Marissa — drafting technical responses below that you can paste into the questionnaire/response email. I’ve also attached the SOC/BAA artifacts we can share.

Technical confirmations (short form):
- Hosted API + BAA: Generally, Hosted API is not the recommended path for customer PHI unless deployed under an enterprise contract that includes VPC/network isolation, customer-managed KMS, and request-body logging disabled. In practice, our BAAs are commonly issued for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Dedicated & Private: FULLY supported for PHI. Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools, network isolation, and RBAC + audit logging. Private (VPC/on-prem) provides the strictest controls including HSM/KMS integration and complete control over persistence.
- Model training: Redwood will NOT use customer request/response data to train or improve models unless the customer explicitly opts-in via contract.
- KMS/HSM: We integrate with customer-managed KMS in cloud (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have an HSM option for on-prem. Customer-managed keys can be used to encrypt persisted artifacts and backups.
- Audit logs & retention: Per-customer audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private with configurable retention windows. We can disable request-body persistence for sensitive workloads.
- SOC 2: Completed Type I (2025-09-01). Type II targeted completion: 2026-08-15 (this is estimate based on current audit schedule). We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type I report and a readiness summary; the Type II report will be available after audit completion.

Attachments to include: Redwood_SOC2_Readiness_Summary.pdf, Redwood_BAA_Template_v1.0.pdf

Suggested next step language to Emily: "We can proceed with Dedicated/Private for HIPAA workloads. Attached is our BAA template and SOC2 readiness summary — please have your security/legal review and let us know any redlines. Happy to set a technical follow-up with our infra/security leads on 5/20 at 11am PT."

LMK if you want me on the call.
— Dev

Hi Emily — thanks for the quick review and for the questionnaire. Attached are the materials Dev mentioned: our BAA template, SOC2 readiness summary, and a completed first-pass of your questionnaire. Highlights below to call out explicitly:

- BAA: We offer BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted BAAs are possible in enterprise cases but typically require VPC + customer-managed KMS + logging disabled.
- PHI: Processing PHI is supported in Dedicated and Private. We do not use request/response data for model training unless you explicitly opt-in.
- SOC 2: Type I completed (2025-09-01). Type II targeted for ~2026-08-15; we’ll share the Type II report as soon as it’s issued.
- KMS/Keys: We support customer-managed keys (AWS/GCP KMS) and HSM for on-prem. You can enforce encryption and disable persistent request logging.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached BAA and questionnaire responses and share any redlines or follow-up Qs.
2) Confirm availability for a 30-min technical follow-up on Wed 5/20 at 11am PT (we’ll include Dev and our infra/security SME).
